worked_solution:
The derivative of the inverse hyperbolic tangent function is given by

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{artanh}⁡x)=\frac{1}{1-{x}^{2}}.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ({e}^{x}-\frac{6}{\operatorname{ln}⁡5(1-{x}^{2})})\text{d}x & =\int {e}^{x}\,\text{d}x-\frac{6}{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}\int \frac{1}{1-{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={e}^{x}-\frac{6}{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}\operatorname{artanh}⁡x+C.\end{aligned}
$$
